# Dave Webster — "Charles Warloe's Garage Clean-up" (2009)

**Status:** VERBATIM SOURCE. Do not edit, tidy, or improve.
Interpretation belongs in [2009-10-26-analysis.md](2009-10-26-analysis.md).

**Provenance:** email from `DWebs49484@aol.com`, subject "Dave          Garage
clean-up", sent 2009-10-26, to `cwarloe@volt.com` and `charles.warloe@gmail.com`.
Recovered from Gmail 2026-09-19. An attachment, `Charles Warloe.docx  Garage.docx`,

old, and fourteen years earlier than the [2023 cleanup notes](2023-07-17-dave-webster-cleanup-notes.md).
Typos, spacing, and capitalization are his.

---

> **Charles Warloe's  Garage Clean-up**
>
> **I.   Preliminary: things that need to be done or asked.**
>
> a.     Do I really want to have a clean and organized garage, and am I willing to work on it till goal reached?
>
> b.     Do I know at least two places I can give my unwanted good items to ie:  Good Will, Salvation Army?  You can get a tax deduction. Make sure this place is open the day you decide to organize garage
>
> c.      Do I have transportation, either car, truck, u-haul to take items in to get rid of them?
>
> d.     Do I have a way to dispose of items that are no good and want to throw away, ie; garbage cans, dump? Make sure that dump is open the day you decide to organize. We don't want any excuses that the dump isn't open. Do I have the transportation such as truck, car,  u-haul to take away items?
>
> Figure out what shelving, storage material that you are going to need purchase
>
> e.     in advance.  Home Depot has a variety of shelving that will meet your needs. You will need to sketch out the wall or walls that you want to put shelving on. Measure area so that you will know how much shelving material to buy. You will need to know how wide you want your shelves to be.  You will need to get an idea of the type of things that you want to put in storage containers so that you will know what size to get and quantity.
>
> f.       Storage boxes are to be clear so that you can see all the items in the box from a distance.  They also may be labeled on side facing you so that you know the contents.
>
> g.     Memorize the model, **Do it now, Everything has a place.**
>
> **II.                Let's Get Started:    Do it Now  Make sure dump, Salvation is open, trucks or whatever you are using to transport materials are ready. Your plan is to have this done in one day or less, so start early in the morning.**
>
> a.     Get cars out of garage
>
> b.     Start at one end of the garage and work toward the other end. Divide up contents of garage into three piles or sections. You will have to make some hard decisions, this can be emotional for some so you have to be brutal on yourself and be logical and honest with yourself.
>
> 1. Pile one: Place in this pile any items that are no good and are to be thrown away.
>
> 2. Pile two. Place in this pile things that you can give to friends, Good Will, Salvation Army etc.
>
> 3. Pile three: These are items that need to be taken into the house and put away.
>
> c. Questions that you can ask to help you determine if you want to keep items.
>
> 1. Have I used this item in the last year, if not get rid of it.
>
> 2. If functional and useful, keep ie. Tools etc.
>
> d. Common excuses at this stage
>
> 1. This will take too long
>
> 2. There is too much to do, glazed eyes start appearing
>
> 3. I need to take a nap
>
> 4. I forgot where the trash can is
>
> 5. I lost the directions to Good Will and the Salvation Army
>
> 6. "I will do it tomorrow"  yeah right!  Get your ass moving.
>
> 7. Am sure you can come up with some good ones.
>
> e. Now that you have the garage divided in 3 piles
>
> 1. Take each pile to either garage, Salvation Army, friends, in house or dump, or Trash can.
>
> f.  Now that you have just the items left that you want to organize.
>
> 1. Get your diagram out and start building shelves
>
> g. Now that your shelves are built you are ready to start placing items on them.
>
> 1. Start at one end of the garage and work your way across.
>
> 2. The items should be place in from the least used at the top descending down to the most used items at easy to reach level.
>
> 3. Items should be placed in locations that are functional for that area of the garage.
>
> 4. If you have loose items put them in your clear storage boxes, and label contents on front side of box facing you.  There are to be no items on the shelves that you can't tell their contents from a distance.
>
> 5. While you are putting items up keep asking yourself "when was the last time I used that" and discard if it doesn't pass the test.
>
> **III.             Now that the garage is organized**
>
> 1. Check to see if everything is where you want it, the least used items at the top, like things go with like things,  things located in area of garage most functional.
>
> 2  Sweep floor, empty trash can. Put unopened trash bag at bottom of trash can, then put trash bag you are going to use over it.
>
> 3. Go get a beer.
>
> **IV.               Quote**
>
> We always overestimate what we can do in a year and under estimate what we can do in 10.
